newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Supreme Court declines to hear Ohio muni case.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Supreme Court declines to hear Ohio muni case.

text.p: The U.S. Supreme Court on Monday declined to hear the second part of a challenge to Ohio's tax on the income of out-of-state municipal bonds.
The refusal marked the second time the high court has declined to take up the case.
In October 1995, the court passed on the first part of the case which sought a declaratory judgment that Ohio's in-state tax exemption on municipal bonds was unconstitutional.

The second part of the case brought by Cleveland-area bondholder Serene Shaper sought a refund of $6,000 in Ohio income taxes the plaintiff paid between 1988 and 1991 on interest earned from her out-of-state municipal bonds.
That refund had been rejected by the Ohio revenue department, the state tax appeals board and finally by the Ohio Supreme Court last August.

Shaper's petition to the U.S. Supreme Court argued that the issue of whether a state could under the commerce clause of the U.S. Constitution "discriminatorily impose" its income tax on other states' municipal bonds "is an issue of overwhelming timeliness and importance."
The petition pointed out that 37 states besides Ohio tax income on out-of-state municipal bonds.
